image_description: A collection of kitchen cutlery arranged on a white cutting board. The set includes various knives (chef's, serrated, paring), a carving fork, kitchen shears, and a honing steel at the top. The specific subject of interest is a meat cleaver located towards the right side of the arrangement, characterized by its large rectangular blade and black handle.

artifact_observations.location: Knife handles (specifically the leftmost fork and adjacent knives)
artifact_observations.reasoning: The black handles exhibit a slightly 'waxy' or overly smooth texture lacking fine micro-scratches or material grain expected in used kitchen tools. This is a common AI smoothing artifact.
The rod of the honing steel appears to merge slightly with the background shadow and lacks a distinct, sharp cylindrical highlight, suggesting slight geometric softness.
The rivets are nearly perfect circles despite the handle being at a slight angle; they should appear as slight ellipses due to perspective projection.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific taxonomy of the knife among the similar-looking chef's knives.
To check for fusion artifacts between the metal tang and the plastic handle, and ensure the blade edge is sharp and distinct from the background.
To verify the physical separation of the overlapping items and correct 3D grounding of the honing steel above the board.
To assess overall noise levels and identify any subtle generative blurring or inconsistent lighting reflections across the metal surfaces.

focus_areas: Edge sharpness and definition against the white background
Consistency of metallic reflections across different knives
Geometric correctness of the honing steel
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'rivet' geometry on the cleaver handle; AI often fails to maintain consistent elliptical perspective on small circular features. Also, verify if the 'steel' look of the blade is consistent with real high-carbon steel or if it has the 'plastic-metal' hybrid sheen common in diffusion models.
